title: Knee examination
stem: Cubicle 15. Mr Chiu, 26, twisted his right knee playing football yesterday: he heard a pop, could not continue, and the knee swelled within an hour. Examine his knee and explain your findings and plan.
notes:
Checked against the Ottawa knee rule (Stiell 1996), BOA/BASK guidance on acute knee injury, and standard examination technique.

Structure: look (gait, alignment, swelling, effusion, quadriceps wasting, scars), feel (temperature, effusion tests — patellar tap for large effusions, sweep/bulge test for small; joint line tenderness; collateral ligaments; patella), move (active and passive flexion and extension, straight-leg raise to test the extensor mechanism), special tests (Lachman — most sensitive for ACL; anterior drawer; posterior sag and drawer for PCL; valgus and varus stress at 0° and 30° for MCL and LCL; McMurray/Thessaly for menisci with caution in acute pain), and neurovascular status. Examine the hip and the other knee.

An acute haemarthrosis within hours after a twisting injury with a pop: ACL rupture (about 70%), patellar dislocation, osteochondral fracture. Ottawa knee rule for X-ray: age 55 or over, isolated patellar tenderness, fibular head tenderness, cannot flex to 90°, or cannot weight bear 4 steps immediately and in the ED. Management: RICE, analgesia, crutches, brace if needed, early physiotherapy, fracture clinic/knee clinic, MRI. A locked knee (meniscal bucket-handle) needs urgent orthopaedic review.

Your notes list the knee exam headings (look, feel, move, special tests) without detail; nothing conflicts.

Perfect script checked against standard knee examination and the Ottawa knee rule, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the forceful McMurray and aspirate-every-haemarthrosis options.

steps.label: Introduce
steps.hint: WIPER: wash hands, introduce, permission, expose both legs, reposition; offer analgesia.

opts.t: Hello, I'm the emergency doctor. I've washed my hands. May I examine your knee? Are you in pain? I can give you something for it.
I need to see both legs from the thighs down, lying on the couch.

steps.label: Examine the knee
steps.hint: Look, feel, move, special tests, neurovascular, and compare with the other side.

Look.t: Walk a few steps if you can; then stand
Look.r: Antalgic gait; can take 4 steps with difficulty.

Look.t: Look for swelling, bruising, wasting and scars
Look.r: Tense swelling of the right knee, no bruising, no scars.

Feel.t: Feel the temperature; patellar tap for an effusion
Feel.r: Warm; large effusion with a positive patellar tap.

Feel.t: Feel the joint lines, collaterals, patella, tibial tuberosity and fibular head
Feel.r: Mild lateral joint line tenderness. No bony tenderness at the patella or fibular head.
Feel.mark: Palpates joint lines and bony landmarks (Ottawa)
Feel.do: feel medialjoint-R & feel lateraljoint-R & feel tibialtub-R,fibula-R

Move.t: Bend and straighten your knee; now lift your straight leg
Move.r: Flexes to 80° (limited by swelling). Straight-leg raise intact — extensor mechanism intact.
Move.mark: Assesses movement and the extensor mechanism

Special tests.t: Lachman test, knee at 20 to 30 degrees
Special tests.r: Increased anterior translation with a soft end-point compared with the left. "A positive Lachman: ACL."

Special tests.t: Valgus and varus stress at 0 and 30 degrees

Complete.t: To complete: distal pulses and sensation, the hip, and the other knee
Complete.r: Pulses and sensation normal; hip normal.
Complete.do: feel dp-R,pt-R | feel hip-R,groin-R | look knee-L

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings and your plan.
steps.label: Present and plan
steps.hint: Haemarthrosis with a positive Lachman: likely ACL rupture. Ottawa rule for X-ray. Plan.

opts.t: An acute haemarthrosis with a positive Lachman: likely an ACL rupture; consider a meniscal injury.
Ottawa knee rule: he can't flex to 90 degrees, so a knee X-ray to exclude a fracture, such as a Segond fracture.
Analgesia, ice, crutches, early physiotherapy, knee clinic and an MRI.

script.say: Hello, I'm the emergency doctor. I've washed my hands. May I examine your knee? Are you in pain? I can give you something for it. I need to see both legs from the thighs down, lying on the couch.
Walk a few steps if you can; then stand. Look for swelling, bruising, wasting and scars. Feel the temperature; patellar tap for an effusion.
script.do: Antalgic gait; can take 4 steps with difficulty. Tense swelling of the right knee, no bruising, no scars. Warm; large effusion with a positive patellar tap.

script.say: Feel the joint lines, collaterals, patella, tibial tuberosity and fibular head. Bend and straighten your knee; now lift your straight leg. Lachman test, knee at 20 to 30 degrees. A positive Lachman: ACL.
script.do: Mild lateral joint line tenderness. No bony tenderness at the patella or fibular head. Flexes to 80° (limited by swelling). Straight-leg raise intact — extensor mechanism intact. Increased anterior translation with a soft end-point compared with the left. "A positive Lachman: ACL."

script.say: Posterior sag and posterior drawer. Valgus and varus stress at 0 and 30 degrees. To complete: distal pulses and sensation, the hip, and the other knee.
script.do: No sag, firm end-point. Stable. Pulses and sensation normal; hip normal.

script.say: An acute haemarthrosis with a positive Lachman: likely an ACL rupture; consider a meniscal injury. Ottawa knee rule: he can't flex to 90 degrees, so a knee X-ray to exclude a fracture, such as a Segond fracture. Analgesia, ice, crutches, early physiotherapy, knee clinic and an MRI.
